title: The Priestly Tribe and Its Work
overview: This chapter traces the family of Levi, Israel's tribe set apart for worship, showing who served as priests, who led the music, and which towns they lived in.

parts.label: Aaron's priestly line (vv. 1-15)
parts.note: Only descendants of Aaron could be priests, so a clear family record mattered, and this line runs from his son Eleazar to a priest taken captive to Babylon. Not everyone listed was high priest, since for a time that office passed to the family of Aaron's other son Ithamar (Eli's family), and it is unclear which Johanan or Azariah verse 10 means.

parts.label: The wider Levite families (vv. 16-30)
parts.note: Levi's three sons, Gershon, Kohath and Merari, head the whole tribe, and this section follows family lines outside Aaron's priestly branch. The Kohath line includes Elkanah, father of the prophet Samuel, and in verse 28 the name of Samuel's eldest son, Joel, seems to have dropped out of the standard Hebrew text through a copying slip, so translations like the NIV restore it.

parts.label: David's temple musicians (vv. 31-47)
parts.note: Once the ark, the sacred chest that stood for God's presence, was settled in Jerusalem, David put Levites in charge of worship music. Three leaders were chosen, one from each branch: Heman, a grandson of Samuel, with Asaph and Ethan beside him; whether they are the Heman and Ethan named on Psalms 88 and 89 is uncertain.

parts.label: Priests and their helpers (vv. 48-53)
parts.note: Most Levites did the practical work of the sanctuary, while only Aaron's descendants offered sacrifices and incense and made atonement, meaning rituals to cover the people's wrongs and restore their standing with God. The short list repeats Aaron's line down to Zadok, the chief priest under David and Solomon.

parts.label: Towns for the Levites (vv. 54-81)
parts.note: Levi received no territory of its own, so the other tribes gave it towns with pastureland scattered across the country, including cities of refuge, where someone who had killed a person by accident could flee for protection. Some names and totals differ from the parallel list in Joshua 21, probably because of copying errors and names that changed over the centuries.

think: Many people care about tracing where they come from; how much do you think your family or background shapes the role you see for yourself?
